item.title: Biggest Client Pays Late, Scared to Lose Them? Kickoff
item.description: Your biggest client pays late again and offers new work on the call. A story about chasing money calmly without fearing the relationship.

item.title: Can I Claim Client Coffee Receipts? The Coat Pocket
item.description: You paid for the client's flat white and a sandwich, and now a crumpled receipt sits in your coat. A calm story about what to keep and who to ask.

item.title: Client Email Takes an Hour? The Microwave Beep at 12:40
item.description: Soup in the microwave, a client email still unsent after an hour. For freelancers who rewrite every message until it sounds wrong. A short story.

item.title: Client Keeps Asking for Raw Files? The Chestnut Stand
item.description: The third message asking for raw files lands while you queue for chestnuts. A calm story for photographers who lose track of what was agreed and paid.

item.title: Counting Stock by Hand All Weekend? The Clipboard at 3 pm
item.description: Saturday afternoon, a clipboard, a stockroom and a lake you're not at. A story for small shop owners who count stock by hand every weekend.

item.title: CSV Brackets for Negatives Won't Sum? The Pickup Line
item.description: The accounting export shows refunds as (120.00) and Excel's total says zero. A quiet school pickup line, a stubborn column, and a calmer way to start the week.

item.title: Finance Team on Holiday, Invoice Unpaid? The Canal Lock
item.description: The client says their finance team is on holiday and your invoice sits unpaid. A calm story about waiting without knowing the next step.

item.title: Cold Emails, No Replies? The Sent Folder on the Bench
item.description: Forty cold emails to potential clients, forty silences. A lunch-hour scene for freelancers who stare at the sent folder and wonder what's wrong with them.

item.title: Missing Security Headers on Your API? The Tool Library
item.description: A scanner report lands with 'missing security headers' in red. Where do you start? A calm story about a Monday, a queue and a clearer next step.

item.title: NAS Backup Failed After Password Change? The Muddy Call
item.description: Your NAS backup quietly stopped after a password change, and you only found out when a client asked for last month's files. A calm story about noticing sooner.

item.title: Overseas Client Won't Pay Your Invoice? The Second Clock
item.description: Your invoice is weeks overdue and the client is eight time zones away. A quiet story about chasing money across borders without begging.

item.title: Project Stuck Waiting on Client Approval? The Held Door
item.description: Three weeks since you sent the draft and the project is frozen. A quiet story about waiting on a slow client, and what a calmer start can change.

item.title: Sick as a Freelancer, No Income? The Thermometer Reading
item.description: Fever on a Thursday morning, no sick pay, rent due on the 1st. A calm story for freelancers who worry about bills the moment they get ill.

item.title: Minimum Call-Out Charge Too Low? The Dripping Tap Fee
item.description: Forty minutes of driving, twenty minutes of work, a quote of 25. If small repair jobs leave you out of pocket, this story about a call-out charge is for you.

item.title: Agency Cut Your Per-Word Rate? The Meter Reader Visit
item.description: The agency email says new rates from next month. You read it twice with a cold coffee. A calm story about what to do before you reply.

item.title: ChatGPT Wrote Your API Code: Is It Secure? The Dual Brake
item.description: You shipped API code ChatGPT helped write, and a client just asked if it's secure. A quiet story about doubt, a second pair of eyes, and calm.

item.title: Always Reacting to Clients? The Garage Wall Calendar
item.description: Your week belongs to whoever emailed last. A waiting-room wall calendar, a quiet question, and a calmer way to plan a freelance year of your own.

item.title: Is Your API Open to CSRF or XSS? The Gala Snack Bar
item.description: Standing in a snack bar queue, you realise you can't say whether your API is open to CSRF or XSS. A calm story about trading that doubt for a clear list.

item.title: Ask a Supplier for Better Prices Without Sounding Rude?
item.description: The price list went up again and you're sitting in the car, drafting an email you keep deleting. A story about asking nicely, and still meaning it.

item.title: Hourly or Per Project as a Freelancer? The Taxi Meter
item.description: Hourly or per project, and you're afraid either one loses you money. A taxi ride, a quote email and a calmer way to decide what to charge.

item.title: Client's Budget Frozen, Invoice Unpaid? The Shoe Rack
item.description: The email says 'our budget is frozen.' Your invoice is 41 days old. A quiet Monday-morning story about answering without begging or vanishing.

item.title: Sunday Night Money Anxiety? The Unzipped Gym Bag
item.description: Every Sunday evening the knot returns: who owes you, what's in the account, are you okay? A quiet story about ending freelancer money anxiety.

item.title: Haven't Rotated API Keys in Years? The Question on Mute
item.description: A client asks when you last rotated your API keys and you go quiet. A calm story about the question, the shrug, and how it can feel afterwards.

item.title: How Long Keep Receipts Self-Employed? The Shredder Aisle
item.description: Standing at the shredder with a box of old receipts, unsure what's safe to bin. A calm story about keeping the right ones, without the guesswork.

item.title: Invoice One Day Overdue: Too Soon to Chase? The Toaster
item.description: Your invoice was due yesterday and nothing has arrived. Is it too soon to say something? A calm story about the day-one wobble, and the quiet after it.

item.title: Invoice 2 Weeks Overdue, Client Quiet? The Sofa Window
item.description: Your invoice is two weeks late and the client has gone quiet. A story about a delivery window, an unsent email, and a calmer way to ask.

item.title: Lost Track of Recruiters and Contacts? The Bike Stand
item.description: A friend offers an intro and you can't remember who you've already thanked or asked. A calm story about losing track of contacts while job hunting.

item.title: Mailchimp Import Failed? The Van Outside the Job
item.description: Mailchimp import failed on a list full of duplicates and bad emails, and the newsletter is due at noon. A calm story about a cleaner way.

item.title: Only Billing 20 Hours a Week? The Weekly Summary Ping
item.description: You work all week but invoice only 20 hours. A quiet Monday tram ride, one phone notification, and the question every freelancer eventually asks.

item.title: Parent Says You Billed Too Many Lessons? The Pedalos
item.description: A parent writes: 'I count fewer lessons than you billed.' You can't prove either way. A quiet story for private tutors about a calmer record.

item.title: Worried Your Password Reset Is Insecure? The Food Truck
item.description: Launch is Monday, you're in a lunch queue, and one worry won't go away: is your password reset flow safe? A calm story about checking before you ship.

item.title: Backup Only Runs When Logged In? The Cottage Kitchen
item.description: Your scheduled backup says it ran, but only on days you stayed logged in. A rainy-week story about trusting the quiet job behind your laptop lid.

item.title: Sent a Quote, Heard Nothing? The Checkout Belt Wait
item.description: You sent the quote on Tuesday. It's Friday and the phone is silent. A calm story about silence, price doubts and knowing your real margin.

item.title: Shared API Keys With a Contractor? The Padlock Aisle
item.description: You pasted the keys into a chat so the contractor could start. Now the contract has ended and you wonder what else is open. A calm story.

item.title: Sorted One Column in Excel, Rows Mixed Up? The Van Call
item.description: You sorted one column in Excel and now names, phones and amounts belong to the wrong people. A story from a parked van, and what calm looks like after.

item.title: Addresses in One Excel Column? The Copy Shop Counter
item.description: Street, zip and city all jammed in one Excel column, and the label run is due today. A short story about a copy shop counter and a calmer way.

item.title: Strange API Log Requests, Did Someone Get In? The Shuttle
item.description: Odd requests from unknown IPs in your API logs, and a conference shuttle bus you can't enjoy. A story about the calm of knowing what was actually checked.

item.title: Supplier Delivered Late Again? The Email at the Loading Door
item.description: The pallet is late for the third time and the customer is asking. How to write to your supplier firmly, without burning a relationship you still need.

item.title: Thank-You Email Sent, No Reply? The Engagement Dinner
item.description: You sent the thank-you email and heard nothing. At a family dinner someone asks who you wrote to, and you can't say. A story about getting calm again.

item.title: Windows Laptop Slow, Desktop Full of Files? The Fan Noise
item.description: Ten minutes before a client call, your laptop roars and the desktop is buried in files. A calm story about the Monday it stops being like that.

item.title: Afraid to Ask Clients for Referrals? The Last Minute
item.description: The project call went well. Your client says 'anything else?' and you say no. A quiet story about the referral ask you keep swallowing.

item.title: Bash Backup Script Failed Silently? The Clinic Corridor
item.description: Your bash backup script ran every night, or so you thought. Then a client asked for old files while you sat in a clinic corridor. A calm story.

item.title: Receipts Still a Mess in November? The Window Cleaner
item.description: It's November and your receipts are still in a shoebox, a phone gallery and three inboxes. A quiet Saturday story about the knock at the door.

item.title: Monthly Retainer: How Much to Charge? The Pot on the Stove
item.description: A client says 'let's make it monthly' and your mind goes blank on the number. A calm story about naming a retainer price without guessing.

item.title: Clients Asking Where Their Photos Are? The Fruit Scale
item.description: Behind on editing and the messages keep coming: 'Any news on our photos?' A quiet story about gallery deadlines you can finally see.

item.title: Country Names Spelled Differently in Excel? The Globe
item.description: Germany, Deutschland, DE and 'germany ' in one column. A calm story about country names spelled differently in a spreadsheet, and the end of the dread.

item.title: CSV Import Keeps Failing on One Bad Row? The Tea Urn
item.description: The import says 'error in file' and nothing else. Somewhere in 1,400 rows hides one bad line, and the doors open in ten minutes. A short story.

item.title: Embarrassed by Your English in Client Emails? Platform 2
item.description: English isn't your first language and client emails make you cringe? A quiet story about the reply you rewrote on a cold platform, and what eased it.

item.title: Excel Remove Duplicates Deleted Wrong Rows? Counter 31
item.description: You clicked Remove Duplicates, saved, and the wrong rows are gone. A calm story about that sinking moment, and a way to clean data without the dread.

item.title: Freelancer Holiday Guilt? Telling Clients: The Auto-Reply
item.description: The flights are booked, the clients don't know yet. A calm story about telling clients you're away without the guilt, and the auto-reply you finally send.
